title: Fonts
subtitle: System-wide families, sizes and rendering
restartingShell: Applying… the shell will restart to use the new font.
menuSaved: Menu font saved. Restart the shell to see it.
footRestart: Open Foot windows only change in a new window.
stillInUse: That family was in use; the system falls back to the default.
sourceUnavailable: Unavailable right now: %1. Showing the rest.
sample: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog 0123456789
system.help: These are the families every app gets when it asks for a generic font: GTK, Qt, browsers, Electron, the Omarchy shell.
role.sans.help: Used by apps and sites asking for sans-serif or system-ui.
role.serif.help: Used by readers, documents and sites asking for serif.
role.monospace.help: The one omarchy font set changes: the Omarchy bar, menus and terminals. Changing it restarts the shell.
metric: Also replace Arial, Helvetica, Times and missing fonts
metric.help: Browsers and documents use your fonts instead of the metric-compatible Liberation fonts and of fonts that are not installed. Can change line breaks in office documents.
reset.help: Removes the plugin's rules and returns gsettings, terminals and Hyprland to their previous values. Installed fonts stay.
reset.confirm: Restore all fonts and rendering to the Omarchy defaults?
apps.scale: Global text scale: %1 px in the shell, factor %2 in GTK. It is set in the Monitor panel, not here.
gtk.interface.help: Menus, buttons and labels in GTK apps; Qt apps follow through the gtk3 theme.
gtk.document.help: Long-form text in apps such as readers and editors.
gtk.monospace.help: Code and embedded terminals in GTK apps.
terminal.label: Family and size (%1)
terminal.help: The Monitor panel's text size control also sets terminal size and overwrites this value.
restartShell.help: Needed for the menu font and for the shell to redraw with new rendering.
hidpiHint: Your display uses scale %1. On HiDPI subpixel smoothing barely helps and GTK 4 ignores it; the HiDPI profile is recommended.
preset.default.help: No plugin rules: Arch and Omarchy defaults apply.
preset.hidpi.help: Grayscale with slight hinting. Best at scale 1.5 or higher.
preset.lcd.help: RGB subpixel with slight hinting, for common monitors at scale 1.
preset.sharp.help: Full hinting and RGB subpixel: crisper outlines, good on low-density screens.
preset.smooth.help: No hinting, grayscale: shapes true to the design, macOS style.
render.antialias.help: Smooths edges. Off leaves jagged text.
render.hinting.help: Fits outlines to the pixel grid for sharper text.
render.autohint.help: Uses FreeType's automatic hinting instead of the font's own instructions.
render.embeddedbitmap.help: Uses bitmap versions some fonts carry for small sizes.
render.hintstyle.help: Slight keeps the design; full favors sharpness.
render.rgba.help: The physical layout of the monitor's subpixels. None = grayscale.
render.lcdfilter.help: Reduces color fringes from subpixel smoothing.
render.note: GTK applies immediately. Other apps, including the shell itself and browsers, change when reopened.
refreshCatalogs.help: Downloads the Google Fonts, Fontsource, Nerd Fonts and Fontshare lists again. They are kept for 7 days.
tip: 1–4 switch tabs · ←/→ too · R reloads · Esc closes
consent: To apply fonts system-wide the plugin will change: fontconfig rules (~/.config/fontconfig), GTK font settings (gsettings), the font lines of your terminal configs, and its own Hyprland file (plus one line in hyprland.lua). Every change is backed up first, and “Restore defaults” undoes it all. Allow?
